param: master-dark bit depth (one knob: 16-bit integer vs 32-bit float); the set's sky flat is a DEPENDENT of the dark (built from dark-subtracted lights) and is rebuilt in each arm, per the ratified rule that a flat calibrates only the frames/masters it was built from
control: web/results/july27/stack_set-03_dark16* — set-03 (249 frames, 1 cull, no cadence gaps, flattest per-set gradients) as originally built
hypothesis: a master dark is a many-frame MEAN whose precision is far finer than one integer step, so 16-bit storage quantizes it into a SENSOR-FIXED pattern subtracted identically into every light — the input to walking noise, which no rejection or cosmetic correction removes

master_level.floor_method: split-half: two independent 100-frame 32-bit means differenced, sigma/2

flat_level.note: quantization is per-pixel random, not low-order, so it vanishes in the flat's 400px regional medians

stack_level.predicted_bounds_meaning: 0.008 = drift fully decorrelates the sensor-fixed pattern (/sqrt(249)); 0.13 = fully coherent

verdict: WIN at the master level, INCONCLUSIVE at the stack level — and the fix is justified on the former. MEASURED: 16-bit quantization is exactly uniform +-0.5 ADU (0.2889 vs theory 0.2887, four figures, zero bias) and inflates the master dark's fixed-pattern residual 0.4213 -> 0.5109 ADU (+21%) against a split-half-measured statistical floor. The stack-level A/B CANNOT resolve it: the whole-frame difference is dominated 28x by registration resampling at star edges (2.06% vs 0.073% in flat sky), i.e. by run-to-run variation rather than the knob. The flat-sky difference (0.073%, sigma ~0.091%) sits near the coherent end of the predicted 0.008-0.13% propagation band, which is CONSISTENT with the quantization pattern surviving the drift, but is not separable from residual run-to-run variation without a same-arm repeat run. No stack-level win is claimed. Fix retained and enforced by check_bitdepth.sh.

param: none — this is the reproducibility FLOOR measured incidentally by the dark-bitdepth A/B: identical frames, identical recipe, two runs of the undistort chain
control: n/a (the two arms of master_dark_bitdepth, whose knob is far below the floor measured here)
hypothesis: the acceptance contract requires a change to be reproducible 'to a documented tolerance' but no number existed for this chain

metrics.geometry: identical (4909x3667, STACKCNT 249 both arms), so the output canvas and member set were stable; the variation is in the interpolation, not the framing

verdict: MEASURED, and it bounds every future stack-level A/B on this chain. The undistort chain is NOT pixel-reproducible between runs: the same frames through the same recipe differ by 2.06% of sky at star edges and 0.073% in flat sky, the difference tracking local gradient (28.4x star-edge/flat-sky ratio) as resampling error does. Consequence: any stack-level comparison claiming an effect below ~0.07% in flat sky or ~2% at star edges is measuring run-to-run noise, not its knob. Bracket such experiments with a SAME-ARM repeat run, not just an A/B.
